title: Proteome analysis of  pig heart tissue to study the molecular consequences of hyperbaric oxygen treatment
projectDescription: The overall goal of the project was to confirm the presence of different energetic states of mitochondrial subpopulations depending on their subcellular localization within cardiomyocytes, i.e., subsarcolemmal (SSM) and interfibrillar mitochondria (IFM). Here we analysed proteomic changes upon treatment of pigs with hyperbaric oxygen.
sampleProcessingProtocol: Heart tissue was minced, treated with 1% Triton-X-100 and centrifuged to separate myofilaments (pellet) from other cellular proteins (supernatant). Pellets were solubilized in buffer EB (10% SDS, 150 mM NaCl, 50 mM Tris-HCl pH 7.6). Supernatants were supplemented to obtain buffer EB. Sonication for 5 s facilitated protein resolubilisation. Samples were centrifuged at 22000xg. Proteins were digested using Filter Aided Sample Preparation (FASP) (Wisniewski et al., 2009) and peptides were acidified with TFA and fractionated on C18/SCX stage tips (Rabsilber et al., 2011). Liquid chromatography / mass spectrometry (LC/MS) was performed on Thermo Scientific™ Q Exactive equipped with an ultra-high-performance liquid chromatography unit (Thermo Easy-nLC) and a Nanospray Flex Ion Source (Thermo Scientific). Peptides were loaded on a C18 reversed-phase precolumn (Thermo Scientific) followed by separation for 30 min to 35% (80% ACN, 0.1% FA) with a second gradient for 5 min to 80% on a with 2.4 µm Reprosil C18 resin (Dr. Maisch GmbH) in-house packed picotip emitter tip (diameter 100 µm, 15 cm from New Objectives) with a flow rate of 300 nl/min. The full MS scan range was 400 to 1400 m/z with resolution of 70000, and an automatic gain control (AGC) value of 1*E6 total ion counts with a maximal ion injection time of 20 ms. Only higher charged ions (2+) were selected for MS/MS scans with a resolution of 17500, an isolation window of 4 m/z and an automatic gain control value set to E5 ions with a maximal ion injection time of 50 ms. MS1 Data were acquired in profile mode.
dataProcessingProtocol: For data analysis MaxQuant 2.0.3.0  (Cox and Mann, 2008), Perseus 1.6.1.3 (Tyranova et al 2016) and Excel (Microsoft Office 2016) were used. N-terminal acetylation (+42.01), and oxidation of methionine (+15.99) were selected as variable modifications and carbamidomethylation (+57.02) on cysteines as a fixed modification. The pig reference proteome database (Uniprot, October 2022, 102557 entries) was used to identify peptides and proteins with a false discovery rate (FDR) less than 1%. Reverse identifications and common contaminants were removed.    Cox J, Mann M. (2008) MaxQuant enables high peptide identification rates, individualized p.p.b.-range mass accuracies and proteome-wide protein quantification. Nat Biotechnol. 26:1367-72.  Tyanova S, Temu T, Sinitcyn P, Carlson A, Hein MY, Geiger T, Mann M, Cox J. (2016)The Perseus computational platform for comprehensive analysis of (prote)omics data. Nat Methods. 13:731-40.
